hook.line: Before growing my TikTok, I took a digital marketing course and learned how to rank.
hook.visual: Handheld selfie-style close-up, the camera swinging toward her face as she talks, with a white pill title 'SEO hack for beginners' with red exclamation marks and faint serif word captions below.

beats.what: Handheld walk-in close-up with the credential story (took a marketing course).
Settles into a seated talking head; calls out that most viewers do not know what ranking is.
Bold claim: hashtags do nothing anymore, it has always been SEO.
Screenshots of TikTok search results pop up around her as proof her videos rank for her niche.
Cut to a new framing: 'now I'm in teacher mode', the actual tip starts.
Large white words 'Content creators tips' animate in above her head as she says to speak your keyword.
Explains that saying the keyword in the first five seconds is what she did at the start of this very video.
Gives an assignment: search your niche and check whether your videos show up.
Big 'SEO' word appears above her head as she says your SEO is broken.
'2??' graphic as she asks viewers to comment 'part two'.

why_it_works: Proof on screen: the search-result screenshots at 50 s show her own videos ranking, which earns trust before the tip.
She points out that the video itself used the technique ('remember at the beginning I said SEO'), a self-referential demo that makes the tip click.
A homework assignment plus 'comment part two' turns viewers into commenters and promises a sequel (5k comments).
weaknesses: The actual tip arrives after about 55 s of setup in a 110 s video; the first shot runs 51 s with no cut.
Captions are a thin, low-contrast serif that is hard to read on the busy background.
Caption is stuffed with dozens of repeated keyword lines, which reads as spam.
for_robert: Use the self-referential payoff: after giving a tip, show that this very reel already did it (Fred could pop in pointing back at the opening line). Get to the tip far faster than her 55 s.
